title: Outside weekend jobs and college dates
summary: Condon let him take Sunday and college dates with a replacement; the band picked up a hundred dollars playing Yale and Connecticut.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now, the policy at Conden's was that if a musician got a job that if it was good for him and made him more money or something if he could get a capable replacement, he could go ahead.

Oh, I went out many times. I'd say - Ed, you mind if I-- I would like to go out. I'd like to get a band; I had lots of offers from booking agents - of course, could you get a group together and I'll send you to Cleveland, Cincinnati - send you around.
And, you used to do that.
Oh, sure. And, I'd pick up some very good money too doing it.
And, you'd spend a lot of Sundays going on one-nighter deals - didn't you?
Oh, yes. We used to play all the colleges in those days. We played many, many - oh, for several years, we played at Yale all the time.
You mean, you'd go down to Washington for a night.

Yes to the Mattari Circle up in Hartford - near Hartford and play up there too on Sunday. he used to go up MANCHESTER Well, the guys in the band were delighted to get the extra work. You know, as hard work as that was, it was always good to pick up a hundred bucks on a Sunday.
Well, you didn't always take the band with you - frequently, you went by yourself.
No, I'd usually take some of the guys out of the band if they wanted to go. I'd take Gene if he wanted to go and Cutty gladly and any of the clarinet players that wanted to go, I'd take.
